claims.claim: Also deals on all kinds of cars spare parts
claims.evidence: Seller text only; photos show an alternator but do not prove the broader claim.

risks.risk: Exact alternator compatibility (vehicle/engine/part number) is not readable from the photos, so it may not fit the buyer’s car.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the alternator label/engraved part number (and/or the connector type) plus the vehicle details the seller claims it fits.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used alternator with unknown compatibility (worst case: may not fit).

risks.risk: Working condition is unknown (alternators can look fine but fail under load).
risks.proof: A video/clip of the alternator being tested (bench test or installed test) showing output voltage/current at idle and with load.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven working (worst case: treat as not working until tested).

risks.risk: Pulley/bearing condition is unknown; noise or wobble may not be visible in still photos.
risks.proof: A short clip spinning the pulley by hand showing smooth rotation and no wobble/noise.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as having unknown mechanical condition (worst case: assume bearing/pulley may be bad).

risks.proof: Bench test results or multimeter readings for charging voltage and ripple (or a tester printout).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as electrically unverified (worst case: assume it may not charge correctly).

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up of the alternator’s label/engraved part number (and any OEM code) so compatibility can be confirmed.
Show a bench test or installed test video with charging voltage readings (idle and with headlights/AC load).
Provide a short clip of the pulley spinning smoothly with no wobble/no grinding noise.
Confirm which exact car/engine it came from (make/model/year/engine code) matching the part number.
response.reason: The photos show an alternator, but the key details needed to price confidently (exact part number/compatibility and whether it works) are not readable or proven.
